item.title: PolyGone Systems microplastics filter launches in Atlantic City
item.description: A water treatment facility in Atlantic City, New Jersey, has become the first in the world to be equipped with a system that removes microplastics from wastewater before it enters the ocean. item.title: China switches on world's largest liquid-air battery
item.description: In China's Qinghai province, the world's largest demonstration facility for liquid-air energy storage (LAES) has been put into operation. The installation uses green electricity to compress air to extreme density, after which it becomes liquid at approximately -190°C. When demand arises, the liquid is reheated, causing it to rapidly expand into gas and drive a turbine that feeds electricity back..

item.description: 103-year-old D-Day veteran Douglas Halley has recovered his lost war medals, just in time for Remembrance Day. item.description: In 2012, street artist Philip Wallisfurth used moss and yoghurt to save a tree in Aachen from a shopping centre: he created the text 'greener living' in two-metre-high moss letters on a construction fence. item.description: In Brevard County, Florida, a '1000-year rainfall' caused flooding in Melbourne, Port Lucie and Palm Bay, among other areas. item.title: 100-year-old Gretchen Sollo surprised with first birthday party at Lowe's
item.description: After 100 years, Gretchen Sollo experienced her first birthday celebration, organized by employees of Lowe's in Bradley, Illinois. Following a stroke, Sollo walked through the store's aisles daily to stay dry and keep moving. item.description: After more than a decade of activism by residents, the Los Angeles City Council voted on October 28 in favor of an ordinance that prohibits oil drilling within city limits. item.description: Poet Andrew Mears from northeast England, a region with the country's highest homelessness rates, came up with the idea in 2025 to ask 100 writers to each write a poem about homelessness. item.description: Bonnie Fay (84) arrived as a patient at Bryn Mawr Village nursing home in Pennsylvania, paralyzed by Guillain-Barré syndrome. During her difficult recovery, she found solace in playing piano, something she had done since age seven. She promised herself she would one day return to play there. item.title: Brown bear population in Spain doubles thanks to protection
item.description: The Cantabrian brown bear has doubled in number over twenty years: from around 140 animals at the start of this century to 370 now. The bears no longer live exclusively in Cantabria, but also in Asturias, León, Galicia and Palencia, across an area of more than 17,000 square kilometres (6,500 square miles). A 2023 study in Conservation Science and Practice...

item.title: Brazil presents world's first fossil fuel phase-out roadmap
item.description: Brazil has become the first country in the world to publish a roadmap for phasing out fossil fuels. The document marks a unique step in international climate policy, making Brazil the first nation to publicly release such a concrete phase-out plan.

item.description: Flag football, long seen as an alternative to tackle football, is gaining strong popularity among girls. According to USA Football, participation by girls aged 6 to 17 has risen 57% over the past decade, reaching over 267,000 participants in 2024. item.title: Italy invests $2.2 million in fighting dog rescue
item.description: Italy has allocated 2 million euros (approximately $2.2 million) to rescue dogs from illegal dogfighting operations and help them recover. The funds will go to shelters and rehabilitation facilities that provide care and behavioral training, enabling traumatized dogs to be rehomed with families. item.title: Atacama Desert blooms in record colors after years of drought
item.description: The Atacama Desert in Chile, normally the driest place on Earth, is covered with some 200 flowering plant species. Some flowers are appearing in places where they haven't been seen since before the year 2000. item.title: Viral doorbell video raises $76,000 for caregiver Suzanna Metcalf
item.description: A doorbell camera video from Castle Rock, Colorado, went viral last year and has since raised more than $76,000 for pizza delivery driver Suzanna Metcalf. When Metcalf came to report an incorrect pizza order to Pastor Neal Seiwert, he noticed she was struggling. item.title: Actor Peter Marinker (85) performs in Krapp's Last Tape despite Alzheimer's
item.description: The 85-year-old actor Peter Marinker returned to the stage this autumn, despite an Alzheimer's diagnosis. He plays the demanding role of Krapp in Samuel Beckett's solo piece Krapp's Last Tape, at the Cockpit Theatre in London. The diagnosis came after difficulties during rehearsals for an earlier production. The performance was supported with an autocue, an earpiece, and extra rehearsal time,...

item.description: The glow-worm is making a comeback in North Yorkshire thanks to the unpaid work of nature enthusiast Peter Cooper. In his spare time, he breeds glow-worms in a garden shed and releases the larvae at Nosterfield Nature Reserve, where the creature has not been seen for a hundred years.
